definitionEn: An area of land used for growing crops or keeping animals.
example: My grandparents run a small farm outside the village with cows and chickens.

definitionEn: A person who owns or works on a farm.
example: The farmer gets up at dawn to feed the animals every single day.

definitionEn: A large area of open land where crops or animals are kept.
example: Children were playing football in the field behind the old school.

definitionEn: A small part of a plant from which a new plant can grow.
example: She carefully placed each seed into the damp soil before watering it.

definitionEn: A plant grown in large amounts for food or for sale.
example: Heavy rain destroyed most of the wheat crop in the northern provinces.

definitionEn: To put seeds, trees or other plants into soil so they can grow.
example: Every spring, the family plants vegetables in the garden behind their house.

definitionEn: To pour water on plants or land so they stay healthy.
example: Farmers must water the fields regularly during long, dry summers.

definitionEn: A wild plant that grows where it is not wanted.
example: If you leave weeds in the vegetable bed, they will steal water and nutrients.

definitionEn: A large farm building used to store hay or keep animals.
example: The old wooden barn behind the house has been empty for years now.

definitionEn: A powerful vehicle used on farms to pull heavy equipment.
example: My uncle drove the tractor across the field to plough the land.

definitionEn: The top layer of earth in which plants grow.
example: This dark soil is rich and perfect for growing tomatoes and beans.

definitionEn: The sweet part of a plant that contains seeds and can be eaten.
example: In late summer the orchard is full of ripe fruit ready to pick.

definitionEn: A plant or part of a plant that people cook and eat as food.
example: We buy fresh vegetables from the market every Sunday morning.

definitionEn: A large farm animal kept for its milk or its meat.
example: The farmer milks the cow early every morning before the sun rises.

definitionEn: A bird kept on farms for its eggs or its meat.
example: The children collect fresh eggs from the chickens every afternoon after school.

definitionEn: A barrier of wood or wire that surrounds a field or garden.
example: The farmer repaired the broken fence to keep the sheep from wandering away.

definitionEn: To cause plants or crops to develop by planting and caring for them.
example: Many farmers in this valley grow rice and corn on small plots.

definitionEn: To break up and turn over earth, usually with a spade or tool.
example: Before planting, the gardener had to dig the soil and remove stones.

definitionEn: A cereal grain used to make flour and bread.
example: The wheat fields turned golden in the late summer sunshine.

definitionEn: Water that falls from clouds in small drops.
example: Without enough rain, the young plants will wither and die quickly.

definitionEn: Able to produce plenty of crops or plant growth.
example: The river valley is fertile, so farmers can grow crops twice a year.

definitionEn: To supply land with water through channels, pipes or sprinklers.
example: The engineers built canals to irrigate the dry plains near the coast.

definitionEn: The process of preparing land and growing crops on it.
example: The cultivation of coffee requires warm temperatures and careful attention.

definitionEn: The system that removes excess water from land or soil.
example: Poor drainage caused the fields to flood after every heavy storm.

definitionEn: To scatter or plant seeds in the ground so they can grow.
example: Farmers sow wheat seeds in autumn so the crop grows through winter.

definitionEn: To cut and gather a ripe crop from the fields.
example: After months of hard work, the farmers finally reap their golden harvest.

definitionEn: To turn over soil with a large tool pulled by a tractor or animal.
example: The old farmer still ploughs his fields with two strong oxen.

definitionEn: The upper layer of soil that contains most of the nutrients plants need.
example: Heavy rain washed away the valuable topsoil from the sloping hillside.

definitionEn: Birds such as chickens and ducks that are kept for their meat or eggs.
example: The poultry farm supplies eggs and meat to several supermarkets across the region.

meaningVi: trang trại sữa, sữa và sản phẩm sữa
definitionEn: A farm or business that produces milk and products made from milk.
example: Our village has a dairy that sells fresh milk and cheese.

definitionEn: An area of land where fruit trees are deliberately grown.
example: We spent the afternoon picking apples in the orchard behind the farmhouse.

definitionEn: A glass building in which plants are grown in warm, controlled conditions.
example: Tomatoes grow faster in a greenhouse because the temperature stays steady.

definitionEn: Animal waste spread on soil to help plants grow.
example: The farmers spread manure over the fields before the spring planting.

definitionEn: The gradual wearing away of soil by wind, water or ice.
example: Planting trees on steep slopes can help prevent soil erosion.

definitionEn: Existing or available in very large quantities.
example: The region's abundant rainfall makes it ideal for growing rice.

definitionEn: The science and practice of farming and producing food.
example: Agriculture employs almost half of the workforce in this rural province.

definitionEn: A young plant grown from a seed, ready to be transplanted.
example: The gardener transplanted the seedlings into larger pots after two weeks.

definitionEn: Grassland where cattle and sheep can graze freely.
example: The cows spend most of the day grazing in the pasture near the river.

definitionEn: A machine that cuts and collects crops from the fields.
example: A modern combine harvester can cut a large field in a single day.

definitionEn: A chemical used to kill unwanted plants such as weeds.
example: Some farmers use herbicide to control weeds, but it can harm wildlife.

definitionEn: To begin to grow, especially from a seed or bulb.
example: The beans began to sprout within a week of being planted in wet soil.

definitionEn: The ability to maintain farming practices without depleting natural resources.
example: Long-term sustainability depends on protecting soil health and conserving water supplies.

definitionEn: Relating to farming, agriculture, or the ownership of agricultural land.
example: The region retains a strongly agrarian character despite rapid urban expansion.

meaningVi: tiểu nông, hộ nông dân nhỏ
definitionEn: A farmer who cultivates a small piece of land, often for subsistence.
example: Smallholders produce much of the country's rice but earn very modest incomes.

definitionEn: Producing just enough food or income to meet a household's basic needs.
example: Many families still practise subsistence farming, growing only what they eat.

definitionEn: The careful management and breeding of crops or livestock.
example: Good husbandry requires attention to animal welfare as well as productivity.

definitionEn: A chemical product, such as a pesticide or fertiliser, used in farming.
example: Excessive agrochemical use can contaminate rivers and harm surrounding ecosystems.

definitionEn: A gradual decline in the quality of land, soil or resources.
example: Overgrazing has caused severe soil degradation across much of the plateau.

definitionEn: The process by which fertile land gradually turns into desert.
example: Desertification threatens farmland as rainfall declines and temperatures continue to rise.

definitionEn: The concentration of salt present in soil or water.
example: Rising salinity has reduced yields in coastal paddies over the past decade.

definitionEn: Capable of succeeding or being profitable and sustainable over time.
example: Small family farms are no longer viable without government support or diversification.

definitionEn: The rate at which a farm or worker produces a given output.
example: Better seed varieties have significantly boosted productivity in the lowland districts.

definitionEn: The introduction of machinery to replace manual labour on farms.
example: Mechanisation has reduced the workforce needed at harvest but increased output.

definitionEn: A fixed limit on how much of a product may be produced or sold.
example: Fishermen complained that the new catch quota would severely limit their income.

definitionEn: The arrangement of renting land or property from its legal owner.
example: Insecure tenancy discourages farmers from investing in long-term soil improvements.

definitionEn: A metric unit of area equal to ten thousand square metres.
example: The cooperative manages nearly three hundred hectares of paddy fields.

definitionEn: A grass grown for its edible grains, such as wheat, barley or rice.
example: Cereal crops supply most of the calories consumed by people worldwide.

definitionEn: The transfer of pollen that enables plants to produce seeds and fruit.
example: Natural pollination by bees increases the yield of many orchard fruits.

definitionEn: A method of growing plants in nutrient-rich water instead of soil.
example: Hydroponics allows urban growers to produce leafy greens throughout the entire year.

definitionEn: Land used mainly for growing crops rather than for grazing.
example: Expanding cropland into forests has accelerated the loss of biodiversity.

definitionEn: Large commercial enterprises that produce, process and sell farm products.
example: Large agribusiness firms now control much of the global grain trade.

definitionEn: A raw agricultural or mineral product that is bought and sold in markets.
example: Coffee is one of the most valuable agricultural commodities traded internationally.

definitionEn: A tax imposed by a government on goods imported from abroad.
example: New tariffs on imported fertiliser raised costs for many local farmers.

definitionEn: A large reserve of goods or materials kept for future use.
example: The government built a stockpile of rice to stabilise prices during the drought.

definitionEn: A severe shortage of food that causes widespread hunger and starvation.
example: Repeated crop failures led to famine in several remote highland villages.

definitionEn: The capacity of crops or farms to recover quickly from shocks.
example: Drought-tolerant varieties improve the resilience of farms in dry regions.

definitionEn: A plant variety developed through selective breeding for desirable traits.
example: This new cultivar matures faster and resists common fungal diseases.

definitionEn: To grow new plants from seeds, cuttings or other parts of existing plants.
example: Gardeners often propagate roses by taking cuttings in early summer.

definitionEn: Describing a plant that lives for several years and regrows each season.
example: Asparagus is a perennial crop that yields for many years after planting.

definitionEn: Describing a plant that completes its life cycle within a single year.
example: Wheat in this region is an annual crop sown in autumn and harvested in summer.

definitionEn: A horizontal underground plant stem that produces roots and new shoots.
example: Ginger is grown from rhizomes, which are planted in loose, well-drained soil.

definitionEn: Hay, straw or green plants fed to livestock during winter or shortages.
example: Farmers stored extra fodder in the barn to feed their cattle through winter.

definitionEn: The practice of letting animals feed on grass in open pasture.
example: Unrestricted grazing has stripped the hillside of vegetation and exposed the rocks.

definitionEn: A small plot of public land rented to individuals for growing vegetables.
example: Retired neighbours spend their mornings tending vegetables on the local allotment.

definitionEn: Organic material from plants or animals, often burned or converted into fuel.
example: Farm waste is converted into biomass to generate electricity for nearby villages.

definitionEn: Relating to the peaceful, idyllic life of the countryside.
example: The novelist romanticised a bucolic village where harvests were celebrated with music and dancing.

definitionEn: A scientist who studies soil management and crop production.
example: The agronomist advised the cooperative to rotate legumes and reduce chemical inputs.

definitionEn: Originating in a particular place rather than being introduced from elsewhere.
example: The autochthonous grape varieties of the region have adapted to its limestone soils.

definitionEn: The cultivation and management of forest trees for timber and conservation.
example: Careful silviculture balances timber production with the protection of watersheds.

definitionEn: The cultivation of grapevines, especially for winemaking.
example: Viticulture has transformed the hillsides into patchworks of vineyards and orchards.

definitionEn: The practice of keeping honeybees to produce honey and wax.
example: Apiculture supports pollination and provides a valuable secondary income for smallholders.

definitionEn: The rearing of silkworms for the production of raw silk.
example: Sericulture once employed thousands of families in the delta before synthetic fibres arrived.

definitionEn: The breeding and rearing of fish in ponds, tanks or enclosures.
example: Pisciculture in the flooded paddies provides both protein and extra income for farmers.

meaningVi: tác động ức chế lẫn nhau giữa thực vật
definitionEn: The chemical inhibition of one plant's growth by compounds released by another.
example: Allelopathy explains why some weeds suppress the germination of neighbouring crops.

definitionEn: Relating to soil, especially its influence on living organisms.
example: Edaphic conditions, such as acidity and drainage, strongly determine which crops thrive.

definitionEn: The scientific study of soils in their natural environment.
example: Pedology helped the surveyors map the fertile alluvial soils of the floodplain.

definitionEn: Collecting leftover crops from fields after the main harvest has been gathered.
example: Gleaning was once a customary right that allowed the poor to gather grain.

definitionEn: A symbiotic association between fungal threads and the roots of a plant.
example: Mycorrhiza helps crops absorb phosphorus more efficiently from poor soils.

definitionEn: Excess nutrients in water that cause algae to bloom and deplete oxygen.
example: Fertiliser runoff has caused severe eutrophication in the lake that supplies drinking water.

definitionEn: A small landowner who farms his own land, historically in England.
example: The yeoman tilled his modest farm and sold surplus grain at the local market.

definitionEn: The rural region lying behind a coastal area, port or major city.
example: Fresh produce from the hinterland is trucked daily to the city's wholesale markets.

meaningVi: độ tơi xốp của đất canh tác
definitionEn: The condition of cultivated soil, especially its texture and suitability for planting.
example: Good tilth allows roots to penetrate easily and water to infiltrate the soil.

definitionEn: An abundant supply of good things, especially food and produce.
example: The autumn market offered a cornucopia of pumpkins, grapes, apples and fresh cheese.

meaningVi: sự phong phú, mùa bội thu
definitionEn: A generous supply of something good, especially natural produce or harvest.
example: The generous bounty of the summer harvest kept the village well fed through winter.

definitionEn: Relating to the countryside, or to the raising of livestock on grassland.
example: Pastoral communities move their herds across the plateau according to the seasons.

meaningVi: đồng quê thanh bình lý tưởng
definitionEn: Idyllically rural and simple, in an idealised, peaceful way.
example: The painter depicted an arcadian landscape of shepherds and golden wheat fields.

definitionEn: Relating to woods or forests, or characterised by trees.
example: We walked along a sylvan path shaded by oaks and beech trees.

definitionEn: To bear fruit, or to make something productive and fruitful.
example: The orchard fructified early this year after an unusually mild spring.

definitionEn: To begin to grow and develop from a seed or spore.
example: Most seeds germinate best when the soil is warm and consistently moist.

definitionEn: A farmer who works land owned by another and pays rent with a share of the crop.
example: The sharecropper gave half of every harvest to the landowner as rent.

definitionEn: A very large agricultural estate, typically worked by dependent labourers.
example: The latifundium dominated the valley, employing hundreds of tenants and seasonal workers.

definitionEn: The legal right to use and enjoy the produce of another's property.
example: The tenant held the usufruct of the orchard for the duration of the lease.

definitionEn: The planting of trees on land that has not recently been forested.
example: Afforestation projects on the barren hills have gradually stabilised the eroded slopes.

definitionEn: The replanting of trees in areas where forests were previously cleared.
example: Reforestation of the watershed has improved water quality and reduced flooding downstream.

definitionEn: To live in or move to the countryside, away from urban life.
example: Retired professionals often rusticate in quiet villages to grow vegetables and keep bees.

definitionEn: The seasonal movement of livestock between lowland and highland pastures.
example: Transhumance routes across the Alps were once travelled by herders every summer.

meaningVi: canh tác sinh học động lực
definitionEn: Describing farming that treats the farm as a self-sustaining living system.
example: The biodynamic vineyard uses compost preparations and follows a lunar planting calendar.

definitionEn: A resting state in which seeds or plants pause growth until conditions improve.
example: Seed dormancy protects the embryo until the rains arrive and the soil softens.

definitionEn: The gradual deterioration of a plant or leaf as it ages.
example: Leaf senescence in autumn releases nutrients that the tree stores in its roots.

meaningVi: thời kỳ sinh học theo mùa
definitionEn: The study of seasonal natural events such as flowering, leafing and migration.
example: Phenology records show that spring blossoms now appear several days earlier than before.

definitionEn: A shoot or bud cut from one plant and grafted onto the rootstock of another.
example: The nurseryman grafted a scion of the heritage apple onto a sturdy rootstock.

definitionEn: The root system of a plant onto which another variety is grafted.
example: Dwarf rootstock produces smaller trees that are easier to harvest by hand.

definitionEn: Producing abundant offspring, crops or new growth; highly fertile.
example: The fecund volcanic soil supports dense forests and bountiful vegetable gardens.

definitionEn: Describing soil that crumbles easily and is easy to work with tools.
example: A friable loam is ideal for root vegetables such as carrots and beetroot.

definitionEn: Fertile soil containing a balanced mixture of sand, silt and clay.
example: The gardener enriched the poor clay with compost to create a crumbly loam.

definitionEn: A soft, lime-rich clay or earth often used to improve acidic farmland.
example: Farmers spread marl over the acidic fields to raise the soil's alkalinity.

definitionEn: An old term for a farmer who cultivates and works the land.
example: The husbandman rose before dawn to tend his sheep and mend the fences.

definitionEn: Shaping hillsides into level steps to grow crops and reduce soil erosion.
example: Centuries of terracing have transformed the mountain slopes into productive rice fields.

definitionEn: A plant adapted to survive in very dry environments with little water.
example: Cacti and succulents are xerophytes that store water in thick stems and leaves.

definitionEn: A plant that tolerates high salt levels in soil or water.
example: Some halophytes can be cultivated on coastal land affected by seawater intrusion.
